sources.title: RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics
supports: HTTP methods, status 200/201/400/401/403/404/409/422/500 and response headers
notes: Sections 9, 10 and 15; 422 is valid HTTP, but is not declared in SYS-008

sources.title: OpenAPI 3.1.1 Specification
supports: Operation response maps, Content-Type, headers and response schema
notes: Paths, Operation, Response and Schema Object definitions

sources.title: RFC 9457 — Problem Details for HTTP APIs
supports: application/problem+json and matching status of HTTP response and problem body

sources.title: Node.js HTTP API
supports: An actual ephemeral HTTP server with http.createServer and server.listen
notes: Node 24 HTTP API; fixture remains an educational stub

claims.statement: An operation's declared HTTP responses and status semantics form the expected behavior for its API clients.
claims.rationale: The IETF standard defines response semantics, while the actual declared matrix is in SYS-008 OpenAPI.

claims.statement: OpenAPI operations can declare response status codes and typed media/header and JSON payload schemas.
claims.locator: Operation Object, Responses Object and Schema Object
claims.rationale: The OpenAPI standard provides the response and schema contract language used by the checker.

claims.statement: RFC 9457 defines application/problem+json and requires a provided status member to match the actual HTTP status.
claims.rationale: The primary standard documents the body-to-wire status consistency invariant.

claims.statement: Node's HTTP server can accept network requests on a listening socket and send HTTP response codes and headers.
claims.rationale: Node's official runtime documentation defines the live HTTP boundary exercised by the lab.
